title: Nick Grewal Named 2026 Entrepreneur of the Year for Building ePropelled
excerpt: The New Hampshire Tech Alliance honored the ePropelled founder at its October 6 Innovation Summit, capping a four-decade career that runs from Nashoba Networks to a global propulsion company with an engineering center in Chennai.
body:
• The New Hampshire Tech Alliance has named Nick Grewal, founder, chairman and CEO of ePropelled, its 2026 Entrepreneur of the Year. He formally received the honor at the organization's Innovation Summit in Nashua on October 6.
  • The award caps a technology career the company's announcement describes as spanning more than five decades of innovation, business leadership and investment — from Nashoba Networks, an advanced networking company acquired by Cisco Systems in 1996, to an active investment career backing more than 40 technology companies.
  • Grewal founded ePropelled in 2018. The company now builds electric propulsion systems, motor controls and intelligent power management for uncrewed vehicles operating in the air, on land and at sea, and holds more than 40 patents across 13 categories.
  • What it means for Indian talent: ePropelled manufactures in New Hampshire but runs engineering and development centers in Coventry, UK, and Chennai, India — putting Indian engineers inside the company's sovereign-supply-chain operations serving aerospace and defense markets.

The New Hampshire Tech Alliance has named Nick Grewal, the founder, chairman and chief executive of propulsion technology company ePropelled, its 2026 Entrepreneur of the Year. Grewal formally received the award during the alliance's Innovation Summit in Nashua on October 6, where the organization cited more than four decades of technology entrepreneurship, investment and business leadership that culminated in ePropelled's growth into a globally integrated technology company.

Two companies, four decades

Grewal's career maps onto two distinct eras of American technology. Before ePropelled, he founded Nashoba Networks, a pioneer in advanced networking technology that Cisco Systems acquired in 1996 — placing him among the early internet-infrastructure builders whose companies were absorbed into Cisco during its 1990s acquisition run. He then built an active investment and advisory career, backing and guiding more than 40 technology companies, many of them based in New Hampshire.

He founded ePropelled in 2018, and the company has grown from an ambitious technology venture into an international operation serving aerospace, defense, maritime, industrial and autonomous-systems customers.

What ePropelled actually builds

ePropelled develops electric propulsion systems, motor control technologies and intelligent power management products. More recently it has expanded into software-defined propulsion architectures that integrate propulsion hardware, power management and connected software into unified operating ecosystems for next-generation autonomous platforms — technology that directly affects range, endurance and operating capabilities of uncrewed vehicles.

The company says it has created more than 40 patents across 13 categories, and that its products are engineered to maximize performance while reducing energy consumption. Dean Marcarelli, ePropelled's chief commercial officer, said Grewal recognized early that autonomy, electrification and intelligent power management would become defining technologies of the coming decades — a bet the company is now collecting on as electrification and autonomous systems converge.

"I am deeply honored to receive this recognition from the New Hampshire Tech Alliance. While the award carries my name, it is ultimately a reflection of the talented people who have helped build ePropelled..."

— Nick Grewal, Founder, Chairman and CEO of ePropelled

The India connection

For Indian readers, the company has a concrete foothold: ePropelled maintains its manufacturing headquarters in New Hampshire alongside engineering and development centers in Coventry, United Kingdom, and Chennai, India. The company says it serves customers worldwide through sovereign supply chains — arrangements in which design, manufacturing and sourcing stay within domestic or allied industrial bases, a structure increasingly prized in defense and aerospace markets. The Chennai center puts Indian engineers inside that chain, working on propulsion and power-management technology for uncrewed aerial, ground and maritime vehicles.

The Times of India's coverage of the award underscores how closely Indian audiences track diaspora founders' trajectories in US technology — and Grewal's arc, from a networking exit in the 1990s to a propulsion company riding the autonomy wave, is the kind of second-act story that resonates well beyond New Hampshire.

What's next

The award arrives as ePropelled pushes deeper into software-defined propulsion architectures, combining hardware, intelligence and connectivity into integrated technology ecosystems. For the company, the recognition also draws attention to its New Hampshire manufacturing base as it expands internationally across aerospace, defense and other markets adopting uncrewed systems.
